subject: Status Broadcast — transient generation throttling & KV-cache miss spike
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: ops@brightapp.io, sam.chen@brightapp.io
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Status Broadcast — transient generation throttling & KV-cache miss spike

Hi Sam / BrightApp ops team,

We’re sending a brief status update: starting ~08:50 PST we observed an increase in 5xx errors and elevated latency for hosted text-generation endpoints in the us-west region that BrightApp routes to. The impact shows as token-generation requests returning timeouts or delayed responses (p95 increased from ~120ms to ~2.1s).

What we know so far:
- Root symptom: sudden surge in KV-cache miss rate combined with an autoscaler reconciliation lag on a subset of GPU pools serving small-sequence workloads.
- Scope: ~3% of customer requests inspected during the window; BrightApp’s traffic patterns show a higher-than-average small-sequence proportion which amplified the effect.
- Immediate mitigation: we’ve shifted affected routing to an adjacent pool and applied an emergency cache-warm policy.

Next steps (ETA):
- We’re keeping the temporary routing in place while we finish the warmup (expected 60–90 minutes).
- We’ll post an incident page with timeline and technical note; link below once live.

Attachments: short service log excerpt and an incident timeline CSV (for your ops team).

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll post periodic updates and the final post-incident note once we complete the investigation.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:26:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Status Broadcast — transient generation throttling & KV-cache miss spike

Copying internal troubleshooting notes here for the thread:

Quick timeline:
- 08:47 PST: KV adaptive rehash job bumped memory pressure on evictor nodes.
- 08:50 PST: autoscaler attempted pod eviction in busy shard; reconciliation loop delayed by a controller race.
- 08:52 PST: token-level queue backlog rose; p99 latency spiked for ~7 minutes.

Actions taken:
- Forced routing change for affected customer traffic to pool-07b (us-west-a).
- Increased cache-warm fill rate; disabled background rehash on the short-lived window.
- Escalated to runtime team to look at controller rate limit setting (possible tuning candidate).

Note: attaching service-log-snippet-20261128.txt (excerpt) and incident-timeline-20261128.csv to the customer message. We should prepare a short mitigation summary for the status page and a follow-up postmortem with RCA and preventive actions (controller fixes, throttling improvements).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Update: service routing stable — ongoing validation (BrightApp impact)

Hi Sam / BrightApp ops,

Quick update: routing change completed at 09:10 PST and we observed traffic normalization over the next 25 minutes. Current measurements: p95 latency back near baseline (~150ms) and error rates returned to expected levels.

What we completed:
- Routed BrightApp traffic to pool-07b to avoid the transient evictor pressure.
- Warmed KV cache for common prefixes to reduce subsequent miss rate.
- Disabled the background rehash job for the affected node group for the remainder of the day.

What we’re doing next:
- Full RCA expected by EOD; we’ll share a post-incident summary with actionable remediation (controller tuning and adding a safety throttle to rehash jobs).
- If you see residual errors or degraded latencies, please send logs or request ids; we’ll prioritize them.

Attachments included: service-log-snippet-20261128.txt, incident-timeline-20261128.csv (short).

Thank you for the prompt reports and patience.

— Marissa

Subject: Post-incident note and next steps — 11/28/2026 generation throttling event

Hi Sam / BrightApp ops,

Final note for the incident we communicated earlier today. Summary: the outage window ran ~08:50–09:17 PST; impact manifested primarily as elevated latencies and transient request timeouts for a subset of hosted generation endpoints.

Preliminary root cause (short): an interaction between our KV rehash background job and the autoscaler controller’s eviction policy caused a temporary spike in memory pressure on evictor nodes, which led to higher-than-expected cache misses and token queueing. This was compounded by a controller reconciliation race that delayed autoscaler stabilization for a few minutes.

Remediation and prevention planned:
- Controller: increase reconciliation backoff and add a safeguard that prevents eviction during high-traffic short windows.
- KV subsystem: add a max-throughput cap to rehash jobs and a faster local warm-start for critical prefixes.
- Observability: new alert on combined metric (evictor pressure + cache-miss-rate) to trigger automatic warm routing.

We’ve opened Jira INFR-1129 for the controller tuning work and will follow up with a detailed postmortem (link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFR-1129). The incident page is live: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2026-11-28-generation-throttle.

If BrightApp would like an on-call debrief with our SREs, reply and we’ll schedule a short session.

Thanks again for working through this with us.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
